installs: One skill directory, skills/typesafe-ai/, holding one SKILL.md and a copy of the licence. Two manifests under .claude-plugin/ wrap it for Claude Code: marketplace.json names one plugin, typesafe, whose source is the repository root, and plugin.json gives that plugin a version and declares no commands, agents, hooks, or servers, so Claude Code discovers the single skill from the skills/ folder and offers it as /typesafe:typesafe-ai. The README installs it with claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills followed by claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai. It also gives npx skills add typesafe-ai/skills --skill typesafe-ai for other agents and says to select an agent when prompted; that names no host and documents no host-specific install, so only Claude Code is recorded. The skill's text points the agent at TypeSafe's live documentation index and cookbooks and describes the three question types and how to compose them; it carries no reference files of its own.
distribution_machinery: None. The tree holds two JSON manifests, a README, one SKILL.md, and two copies of one licence file; there is no install script, hook, or other program.
not_a_system: Owns no state it reads back and does no enforced work: the repository contains no code at all, and everything the skill causes is done by the host agent following one document. The TypeSafe API the document describes is a separate operational service with its own boundary, and the Jev 1.13 model behind it is a separate reviewed model record. This catalog's own maintenance scripts call that API, so the record rests only on the repository's tree and first-party install documentation.
